passages.text: When the Canaanite king of Arad, who lived in the Negev, heard that Israel was coming along the road to Atharim, he attacked Israel and captured some prisoners.
passages.sermon:
The Canaanite king of Arad lived in the Negev.
He heard that Israel was coming along the road to Atharim.
He attacked Israel.
He captured some prisoners from Israel.
passages.original: וַיִּשְׁמַ֞ע הַכְּנַעֲנִ֤י מֶֽלֶךְ־ עֲרָד֙ יֹשֵׁ֣ב הַנֶּ֔גֶב כִּ֚י בָּ֣א יִשְׂרָאֵ֔ל דֶּ֖רֶךְ הָאֲתָרִ֑ים וַיִּלָּ֙חֶם֙ בְּיִשְׂרָאֵ֔ל וַיִּ֥שְׁבְּ׀ מִמֶּ֖נּוּ שֶֽׁבִי׃

passages.text: So Israel made a vow to the LORD: “If You will deliver this people into our hands, we will devote their cities to destruction.”
passages.sermon:
Israel was a nation led by God.
Israel faced enemies in the land.
Israel made a vow to the LORD.
Israel said to the LORD, “If You deliver this people into our hands, we will destroy their cities.”
passages.original: וַיִּדַּ֨ר יִשְׂרָאֵ֥ל נֶ֛דֶר לַֽיהוָ֖ה וַיֹּאמַ֑ר אִם־ נָתֹ֨ן תִּתֵּ֜ן אֶת־ הָעָ֤ם הַזֶּה֙ בְּיָדִ֔י וְהַֽחֲרַמְתִּ֖י אֶת־ עָרֵיהֶֽם׃

passages.text: And the LORD heard Israel’s plea and delivered up the Canaanites. Israel devoted them and their cities to destruction; so they named the place Hormah.
passages.sermon:
The LORD listened to Israel’s plea.
The LORD gave the Canaanites to Israel.
Israel destroyed the Canaanites.
Israel destroyed their cities.
Israel named the place Hormah.
passages.original: וַיִּשְׁמַ֨ע יְהוָ֜ה בְּק֣וֹל יִשְׂרָאֵ֗ל וַיִּתֵּן֙ אֶת־ הַֽכְּנַעֲנִ֔י וַיַּחֲרֵ֥ם אֶתְהֶ֖ם וְאֶת־ עָרֵיהֶ֑ם וַיִּקְרָ֥א שֵׁם־ הַמָּק֖וֹם חָרְמָֽה׃פ

passages.text: Then they set out from Mount Hor along the route to the Red Sea, in order to bypass the land of Edom. But the people grew impatient on the journey and spoke against God and against Moses: “Why have you led us up out of Egypt to die in the wilderness? There is no bread or water, and we detest this wretched food!”
passages.sermon:
The people of Israel left Mount Hor.
They traveled by the road to the Red Sea.
They wanted to go around the land of Edom.
The people became impatient on the way.
The people spoke against God.
The people spoke against Moses.
They said, “Why did you bring us out of Egypt?
Did you bring us here to die in the wilderness?
There is no bread here.
There is no water here.
We hate this miserable food.”
passages.original: וַיִּסְע֞וּ מֵהֹ֤ר הָהָר֙ דֶּ֣רֶךְ יַם־ ס֔וּף לִסְבֹ֖ב אֶת־ אֶ֣רֶץ אֱד֑וֹם וַתִּקְצַ֥ר נֶֽפֶשׁ־ הָעָ֖ם בַּדָּֽרֶךְ׃ וַיְדַבֵּ֣ר הָעָ֗ם בֵּֽאלֹהִים֮ וּבְמֹשֶׁה֒ לָמָ֤ה הֶֽעֱלִיתֻ֙נוּ֙ מִמִּצְרַ֔יִם לָמ֖וּת בַּמִּדְבָּ֑ר כִּ֣י אֵ֥ין לֶ֙חֶם֙ וְאֵ֣ין מַ֔יִם וְנַפְשֵׁ֣נוּ קָ֔צָה בַּלֶּ֖חֶם הַקְּלֹקֵֽל׃

passages.text: So the LORD sent venomous snakes among the people, and many of the Israelites were bitten and died.
passages.sermon:
The LORD is God over Israel.
The LORD sent venomous snakes among the people of Israel.
The snakes bit the people.
Many Israelites died.
passages.original: וַיְשַׁלַּ֨ח יְהוָ֜ה בָּעָ֗ם אֵ֚ת הַנְּחָשִׁ֣ים הַשְּׂרָפִ֔ים וַֽיְנַשְּׁכ֖וּ אֶת־ הָעָ֑ם וַיָּ֥מָת עַם־ רָ֖ב מִיִּשְׂרָאֵֽל׃

passages.text: Then the people came to Moses and said, “We have sinned by speaking against the LORD and against you. Intercede with the LORD so He will take the snakes away from us.” So Moses interceded for the people.
passages.sermon:
The people of Israel came to Moses.
They said, “We have sinned.”
They said, “We spoke against the LORD.”
They said, “We spoke against you.”
They said, “Pray to the LORD for us.”
They said, “Ask Him to take the snakes away from us.”
Moses prayed for the people.
passages.original: וַיָּבֹא֩ הָעָ֨ם אֶל־ מֹשֶׁ֜ה וַיֹּאמְר֣וּ חָטָ֗אנוּ כִּֽי־ דִבַּ֤רְנוּ בַֽיהוָה֙ וָבָ֔ךְ הִתְפַּלֵּל֙ אֶל־ יְהוָ֔ה וְיָסֵ֥ר מֵעָלֵ֖ינוּ אֶת־ הַנָּחָ֑שׁ וַיִּתְפַּלֵּ֥ל מֹשֶׁ֖ה בְּעַ֥ד הָעָֽם׃

passages.text: Then the LORD said to Moses, “Make a fiery serpent and mount it on a pole. When anyone who is bitten looks at it, he will live.”
passages.sermon:
The LORD spoke to Moses.
The LORD is God.
The LORD commanded Moses.
The LORD said, "Make a fiery serpent."
The LORD said, "Set the serpent on a pole."
The LORD said, "If a person is bitten by a snake, he must look at the serpent on the pole."
The LORD said, "If he looks at the serpent, he will live."
passages.original: וַיֹּ֨אמֶר יְהוָ֜ה אֶל־ מֹשֶׁ֗ה עֲשֵׂ֤ה לְךָ֙ שָׂרָ֔ף וְשִׂ֥ים אֹת֖וֹ עַל־ נֵ֑ס וְהָיָה֙ כָּל־ הַנָּשׁ֔וּךְ וְרָאָ֥ה אֹת֖וֹ וָחָֽי׃

passages.text: So Moses made a bronze snake and mounted it on a pole. If anyone who was bitten looked at the bronze snake, he would live.
passages.sermon:
Moses was the leader of the Israelites.
God told Moses to make a bronze snake.
Moses made a snake out of bronze.
Moses put the bronze snake on a pole.
Some people were bitten by snakes.
If a person was bitten by a snake, he could look at the bronze snake.
If the bitten person looked at the bronze snake, he lived.
passages.original: וַיַּ֤עַשׂ מֹשֶׁה֙ נְחַ֣שׁ נְחֹ֔שֶׁת וַיְשִׂמֵ֖הוּ עַל־ הַנֵּ֑ס וְהָיָ֗ה אִם־ נָשַׁ֤ךְ הַנָּחָשׁ֙ אֶת־ אִ֔ישׁ וְהִבִּ֛יט אֶל־ נְחַ֥שׁ הַנְּחֹ֖שֶׁת וָחָֽי׃

passages.text: Then the Israelites set out and camped at Oboth.
passages.sermon: The Israelites were God's chosen people.\r\nThey set out on their journey.\r\nThey camped at a place called Oboth.
passages.original: וַיִּסְע֖וּ בְּנֵ֣י יִשְׂרָאֵ֑ל וַֽיַּחֲנ֖וּ בְּאֹבֹֽת׃

passages.text: They journeyed from Oboth and camped at Iye-abarim in the wilderness opposite Moab to the east.
passages.sermon:
The Israelites traveled from Oboth.
They camped at Iye-abarim.
Iye-abarim is in the wilderness.
This wilderness is across from Moab.
It is to the east.
passages.original: וַיִּסְע֖וּ מֵאֹבֹ֑ת וַֽיַּחֲנ֞וּ בְּעִיֵּ֣י הָֽעֲבָרִ֗ים בַּמִּדְבָּר֙ אֲשֶׁר֙ עַל־ פְּנֵ֣י מוֹאָ֔ב מִמִּזְרַ֖ח הַשָּֽׁמֶשׁ׃

passages.text: From there they set out and camped in the Valley of Zered.
passages.sermon:
The Israelites were traveling in the wilderness.
They left their previous camp.
They set out from that place.
They camped in the Valley of Zered.
passages.original: מִשָּׁ֖ם נָסָ֑עוּ וַֽיַּחֲנ֖וּ בְּנַ֥חַל זָֽרֶד׃

passages.text: From there they moved on and camped on the other side of the Arnon, in the wilderness that extends into the Amorite territory. Now the Arnon is the border between the Moabites and the Amorites.
passages.sermon:
The Israelites left their previous camp.
They traveled to a new place.
They camped on the other side of the Arnon River.
This place was in the wilderness.
The wilderness stretches into the land of the Amorites.
The Arnon River forms a border.
This border separates the land of Moab from the land of the Amorites.
passages.original: מִשָּׁם֮ נָסָעוּ֒ וַֽיַּחֲנ֗וּ מֵעֵ֤בֶר אַרְנוֹן֙ אֲשֶׁ֣ר בַּמִּדְבָּ֔ר הַיֹּצֵ֖א מִגְּב֣וּל הָֽאֱמֹרִ֑י כִּ֤י אַרְנוֹן֙ גְּב֣וּל מוֹאָ֔ב בֵּ֥ין מוֹאָ֖ב וּבֵ֥ין הָאֱמֹרִֽי׃

passages.text: Therefore it is stated in the Book of the Wars of the LORD: “Waheb in Suphah and the wadis of the Arnon, even the slopes of the wadis that extend to the site of Ar and lie along the border of Moab.”
passages.sermon:
The Book of the Wars of the LORD records important events.
This book mentions Waheb in Suphah.
It also mentions the wadis of the Arnon.
The slopes of these wadis reach the site of Ar.
These slopes lie along the border of Moab.
passages.original: עַל־ כֵּן֙ יֵֽאָמַ֔ר בְּסֵ֖פֶר מִלְחֲמֹ֣ת יְהוָ֑ה אֶת־ וָהֵ֣ב בְּסוּפָ֔ה וְאֶת־ הַנְּחָלִ֖ים אַרְנֽוֹן׃ וְאֶ֙שֶׁד֙ הַנְּחָלִ֔ים אֲשֶׁ֥ר נָטָ֖ה לְשֶׁ֣בֶת עָ֑ר וְנִשְׁעַ֖ן לִגְב֥וּל מוֹאָֽב׃

passages.text: From there they went on to Beer, the well where the LORD said to Moses, “Gather the people so that I may give them water.”
passages.sermon:
The Israelites traveled from their previous camp.
They went to a place called Beer.
Beer is a well.
The LORD spoke to Moses at Beer.
The LORD said to Moses, “Gather the people.”
The LORD said, “I will give them water.”
passages.original: וּמִשָּׁ֖ם בְּאֵ֑רָה הִ֣וא הַבְּאֵ֗ר אֲשֶׁ֨ר אָמַ֤ר יְהוָה֙ לְמֹשֶׁ֔ה אֱסֹף֙ אֶת־ הָעָ֔ם וְאֶתְּנָ֥ה לָהֶ֖ם מָֽיִם׃ס

passages.text: Then Israel sang this song: “Spring up, O well, all of you sing to it!
passages.sermon:
The people of Israel traveled in the wilderness.
God told Moses to gather the people.
God promised to give them water.
God provided a well for the people.
Then Israel sang a song.
They said, “Spring up, O well.”
They called everyone to sing to the well.
passages.original: אָ֚ז יָשִׁ֣יר יִשְׂרָאֵ֔ל אֶת־ הַשִּׁירָ֖ה הַזֹּ֑את עֲלִ֥י בְאֵ֖ר עֱנוּ־ לָֽהּ׃

passages.text: The princes dug the well; the nobles of the people hollowed it out with their scepters and with their staffs.” From the wilderness the Israelites went on to Mattanah, and from Mattanah to Nahaliel, and from Nahaliel to Bamoth, and from Bamoth to the valley in Moab where the top of Pisgah overlooks the wasteland.
passages.sermon:
Israel had leaders called princes.
These princes dug a well.
The nobles of the people helped them.
The nobles used their scepters and their staffs to hollow out the well.
After this, the Israelites left the wilderness.
They traveled to a place called Mattanah.
From Mattanah, they went to Nahaliel.
From Nahaliel, they went to Bamoth.
From Bamoth, they went to a valley in Moab.
This valley is near the top of Pisgah.
Pisgah overlooks the wasteland.
passages.original: בְּאֵ֞ר חֲפָר֣וּהָ שָׂרִ֗ים כָּר֙וּהָ֙ נְדִיבֵ֣י הָעָ֔ם בִּמְחֹקֵ֖ק בְּמִשְׁעֲנֹתָ֑ם וּמִמִּדְבָּ֖ר מַתָּנָֽה׃ וּמִמַּתָּנָ֖ה נַחֲלִיאֵ֑ל וּמִנַּחֲלִיאֵ֖ל בָּמֽוֹת׃ וּמִבָּמ֗וֹת הַגַּיְא֙ אֲשֶׁר֙ בִּשְׂדֵ֣ה מוֹאָ֔ב רֹ֖אשׁ הַפִּסְגָּ֑ה וְנִשְׁקָ֖פָה עַל־ פְּנֵ֥י הַיְשִׁימֹֽן׃פ

passages.text: Then Israel sent messengers to Sihon king of the Amorites, saying, “Let us pass through your land. We will not cut through any field or vineyard, or drink water from any well. We will stay on the King’s Highway until we have passed through your territory.”
passages.sermon:
Israel was a nation led by Moses.
Israel wanted to travel through the land of the Amorites.
Sihon was the king of the Amorites.
Israel sent messengers to Sihon.
The messengers spoke to Sihon.
They said, "Let us pass through your land."
They promised, "We will not go into any field."
They said, "We will not enter any vineyard."
They promised, "We will not drink water from any well."
They said, "We will walk only on the King’s Highway."
They promised, "We will stay on the road until we have passed through your territory."
passages.original: וַיִּשְׁלַ֤ח יִשְׂרָאֵל֙ מַלְאָכִ֔ים אֶל־ סִיחֹ֥ן מֶֽלֶךְ־ הָאֱמֹרִ֖י לֵאמֹֽר׃ אֶעְבְּרָ֣ה בְאַרְצֶ֗ךָ לֹ֤א נִטֶּה֙ בְּשָׂדֶ֣ה וּבְכֶ֔רֶם לֹ֥א נִשְׁתֶּ֖ה מֵ֣י בְאֵ֑ר בְּדֶ֤רֶךְ הַמֶּ֙לֶךְ֙ נֵלֵ֔ךְ עַ֥ד אֲשֶֽׁר־ נַעֲבֹ֖ר גְּבֻלֶֽךָ׃

passages.text: But Sihon would not let Israel pass through his territory. Instead, he gathered his whole army and went out to confront Israel in the wilderness. When he came to Jahaz, he fought against Israel.
passages.sermon:
Sihon was the king of the Amorites.
Israel wanted to pass through Sihon's territory.
Sihon refused to let Israel pass through his land.
Sihon gathered all his people.
Sihon led his army out to meet Israel in the wilderness.
Sihon came to Jahaz.
Sihon fought against Israel at Jahaz.
passages.original: וְלֹא־ נָתַ֨ן סִיחֹ֣ן אֶת־ יִשְׂרָאֵל֮ עֲבֹ֣ר בִּגְבֻלוֹ֒ וַיֶּאֱסֹ֨ף סִיחֹ֜ן אֶת־ כָּל־ עַמּ֗וֹ וַיֵּצֵ֞א לִקְרַ֤את יִשְׂרָאֵל֙ הַמִּדְבָּ֔רָה וַיָּבֹ֖א יָ֑הְצָה וַיִּלָּ֖חֶם בְּיִשְׂרָאֵֽל׃

passages.text: And Israel put him to the sword and took possession of his land, from the Arnon to the Jabbok—but only up to the border of the Ammonites, because it was fortified.
passages.sermon:
Israel fought Sihon, king of the Amorites.
Israel defeated Sihon with the sword.
Israel took Sihon's land.
Israel took the land from the Arnon River to the Jabbok River.
Israel did not take land from the Ammonites.
The border of the Ammonites was strong and fortified.
passages.original: וַיַּכֵּ֥הוּ יִשְׂרָאֵ֖ל לְפִי־ חָ֑רֶב וַיִּירַ֨שׁ אֶת־ אַרְצ֜וֹ מֵֽאַרְנֹ֗ן עַד־ יַבֹּק֙ עַד־ בְּנֵ֣י עַמּ֔וֹן כִּ֣י עַ֔ז גְּב֖וּל בְּנֵ֥י עַמּֽוֹן׃

passages.text: Israel captured all the cities of the Amorites and occupied them, including Heshbon and all its villages.
passages.sermon:
Israel fought against the Amorites.
Israel captured all the cities of the Amorites.
Israel took control of Heshbon.
Israel also took control of all the villages around Heshbon.
Israel lived in all these Amorite cities and villages.
passages.original: וַיִּקַּח֙ יִשְׂרָאֵ֔ל אֵ֥ת כָּל־ הֶעָרִ֖ים הָאֵ֑לֶּה וַיֵּ֤שֶׁב יִשְׂרָאֵל֙ בְּכָל־ עָרֵ֣י הָֽאֱמֹרִ֔י בְּחֶשְׁבּ֖וֹן וּבְכָל־ בְּנֹתֶֽיהָ׃

passages.text: Heshbon was the city of Sihon king of the Amorites, who had fought against the former king of Moab and taken all his land as far as the Arnon.
passages.sermon:
Heshbon was a city.
Sihon was king of the Amorites.
Heshbon belonged to Sihon.
Sihon fought against the former king of Moab.
Sihon took all the land of Moab’s king.
He took the land up to the Arnon River.
passages.original: כִּ֣י חֶשְׁבּ֔וֹן עִ֗יר סִיחֹ֛ן מֶ֥לֶךְ הָאֱמֹרִ֖י הִ֑וא וְה֣וּא נִלְחַ֗ם בְּמֶ֤לֶךְ מוֹאָב֙ הָֽרִאשׁ֔וֹן וַיִּקַּ֧ח אֶת־ כָּל־ אַרְצ֛וֹ מִיָּד֖וֹ עַד־ אַרְנֹֽן׃

passages.text: That is why the poets say: “Come to Heshbon, let it be rebuilt; let the city of Sihon be restored.
passages.sermon:
The poets speak about Heshbon.
They say, “Come to Heshbon.
Let us rebuild it.
Let us restore the city of Sihon.”
passages.original: עַל־ כֵּ֛ן יֹאמְר֥וּ הַמֹּשְׁלִ֖ים בֹּ֣אוּ חֶשְׁבּ֑וֹן תִּבָּנֶ֥ה וְתִכּוֹנֵ֖ן עִ֥יר סִיחֽוֹן׃

passages.text: For a fire went out from Heshbon, a blaze from the city of Sihon. It consumed Ar of Moab, the rulers of Arnon’s heights.
passages.sermon:
Heshbon was the city of Sihon.
Sihon was king of the Amorites.
A fire went out from Heshbon.
A blaze came from the city of Sihon.
The fire consumed Ar of Moab.
The fire destroyed the rulers of the heights of Arnon.
passages.original: כִּי־ אֵשׁ֙ יָֽצְאָ֣ה מֵֽחֶשְׁבּ֔וֹן לֶהָבָ֖ה מִקִּרְיַ֣ת סִיחֹ֑ן אָֽכְלָה֙ עָ֣ר מוֹאָ֔ב בַּעֲלֵ֖י בָּמ֥וֹת אַרְנֹֽן׃

passages.text: Woe to you, O Moab! You are destroyed, O people of Chemosh! He gave up his sons as refugees, and his daughters into captivity to Sihon king of the Amorites.
passages.sermon:
Moab was a nation.
Chemosh was the god of Moab.
The people of Moab worshiped Chemosh.
Disaster came to Moab.
Moab was destroyed.
The people of Chemosh suffered defeat.
Chemosh could not save his people.
Moab’s sons became refugees.
Moab’s daughters went into captivity.
Sihon was king of the Amorites.
Sihon took Moab’s sons and daughters.
Sihon ruled over them.
passages.original: אוֹי־ לְךָ֣ מוֹאָ֔ב אָבַ֖דְתָּ עַם־ כְּמ֑וֹשׁ נָתַ֨ן בָּנָ֤יו פְּלֵיטִם֙ וּבְנֹתָ֣יו בַּשְּׁבִ֔ית לְמֶ֥לֶךְ אֱמֹרִ֖י סִיחֽוֹן׃

passages.text: But we have overthrown them; Heshbon is destroyed as far as Dibon. We demolished them as far as Nophah, which reaches to Medeba.”
passages.sermon:
Israel fought against the Amorites.
We overthrew the Amorites.
We destroyed Heshbon.
The destruction reached as far as Dibon.
We demolished them as far as Nophah.
Nophah extends to Medeba.
passages.original: וַנִּירָ֛ם אָבַ֥ד חֶשְׁבּ֖וֹן עַד־ דִּיב֑וֹן וַנַּשִּׁ֣ים עַד־ נֹ֔פַח אֲשֶׁ֖רׄ עַד־ מֵֽידְבָֽא׃

passages.text: So Israel lived in the land of the Amorites.
passages.sermon:
Israel was a people led by God.
The Amorites were a nation living in Canaan.
Israel entered the land of the Amorites.
Israel settled there.
Israel lived in the land of the Amorites.
passages.original: וַיֵּ֙שֶׁב֙ יִשְׂרָאֵ֔ל בְּאֶ֖רֶץ הָאֱמֹרִֽי׃

passages.text: After Moses had sent spies to Jazer, Israel captured its villages and drove out the Amorites who were there.
passages.sermon:
Moses was the leader of Israel.
Moses sent spies to Jazer.
Israel captured the villages of Jazer.
Israel drove out the Amorites who lived there.
passages.original: וַיִּשְׁלַ֤ח מֹשֶׁה֙ לְרַגֵּ֣ל אֶת־ יַעְזֵ֔ר וַֽיִּלְכְּד֖וּ בְּנֹתֶ֑יהָ וַיִּירֶשׁ אֶת־ הָאֱמֹרִ֥י אֲשֶׁר־ שָֽׁם׃

passages.text: Then they turned and went up the road to Bashan, and Og king of Bashan and his whole army came out to meet them in battle at Edrei.
passages.sermon:
Israel was traveling.
They turned.
They went up the road to Bashan.
Og was the king of Bashan.
Og came out to meet Israel.
Og brought his whole army with him.
Og and his army came to fight Israel.
They met Israel in battle at Edrei.
passages.original: וַיִּפְנוּ֙ וַֽיַּעֲל֔וּ דֶּ֖רֶךְ הַבָּשָׁ֑ן וַיֵּצֵ֣א עוֹג֩ מֶֽלֶךְ־ הַבָּשָׁ֨ן לִקְרָאתָ֜ם ה֧וּא וְכָל־ עַמּ֛וֹ לַמִּלְחָמָ֖ה אֶדְרֶֽעִי׃

passages.text: But the LORD said to Moses, “Do not fear him, for I have delivered him into your hand, along with all his people and his land. Do to him as you did to Sihon king of the Amorites, who lived in Heshbon.”
passages.sermon:
The LORD spoke to Moses.
The LORD said, “Do not be afraid of Og, king of Bashan.
I have given Og into your hand.
I have given all his people into your hand.
I have given his land into your hand.
Treat Og as you treated Sihon.
Sihon was king of the Amorites.
Sihon lived in Heshbon.”
passages.original: וַיֹּ֨אמֶר יְהוָ֤ה אֶל־ מֹשֶׁה֙ אַל־ תִּירָ֣א אֹת֔וֹ כִּ֣י בְיָדְךָ֞ נָתַ֧תִּי אֹת֛וֹ וְאֶת־ כָּל־ עַמּ֖וֹ וְאֶת־ אַרְצ֑וֹ וְעָשִׂ֣יתָ לּ֔וֹ כַּאֲשֶׁ֣ר עָשִׂ֗יתָ לְסִיחֹן֙ מֶ֣לֶךְ הָֽאֱמֹרִ֔י אֲשֶׁ֥ר יוֹשֵׁ֖ב בְּחֶשְׁבּֽוֹן׃

passages.text: So they struck down Og, along with his sons and his whole army, until no remnant was left. And they took possession of his land.
passages.sermon:
The Israelites fought against Og.
Og was the king of Bashan.
The Israelites attacked Og.
They killed Og.
They killed Og’s sons.
They killed all of Og’s people.
No one from Og’s people remained alive.
The Israelites took Og’s land.
passages.original: וַיַּכּ֨וּ אֹת֤וֹ וְאֶת־ בָּנָיו֙ וְאֶת־ כָּל־ עַמּ֔וֹ עַד־ בִּלְתִּ֥י הִשְׁאִֽיר־ ל֖וֹ שָׂרִ֑יד וַיִּֽירְשׁ֖וּ אֶת־ אַרְצֽוֹ׃
